utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could we have the case called, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is the contempt case against Ljube Krstevski, case number IT-04-82-R77.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Krstevski, I just want to inquire as to whether you understand what is being said in a language of your --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: And we recognise, for the record, for the Prosecution, Mr. Dan Saxon. Anyone else needs to be mentioned here, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm accompanied today by my colleague, Meritxell Regue, and our case manager, Ms. Lakshima Walpita.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. This is an initial appearance. That means we have to go through with certain protocol. The first thing I need to ask is to identify you, Mr. Krstevski, so if you kindly stand up. Could you state for me your full name and date and place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ljube Krstevski, born on 19th of February, 1960, in the village of Dracevo, Skopje, Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: And your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Krstevski. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: And I understand that there is representation for Mr. Krstevski as well. Could you please identify yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEMPERDICK
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour, my name is Kemperdick, Christian Kemperdick. I'm sorry, Your Honour. My name is Kemperdick, Christian Kemperdick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Kemperdick.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEMPERDICK
utterances.text: Yes. Any further need for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I think that will suffice for now. Thank you very much, Mr. Kemperdick.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEMPERDICK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Krstevski, this I understand Mr. Kemperdick is your assigned counsel for this case. Have you had time to consult with him before this initial appearance?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: And you are happy with his representation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down. At this point at an initial appearance, we would normally move into identifying the indictment and have that recognised, and also note whatever plea the accused would like to enter, but I understand that there may be a movement on the part of the Prosecution. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, after some discussions today between myself and counsel for the accused, the Prosecution would now move -- make an oral motion to withdraw the indictment that is in effect against Mr. Krstevski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Saxon. In light of a motion of this nature, I don't now see the need to have the indictment either read out or otherwise recognised by Mr. Krstevski, or to proceed in entering of a plea. However, as both Mr. Saxon and Mr. Kemperdick are aware, it is not for me to act upon the oral motion to withdraw the indictment. Since the case has now been assigned to the Trial Bench, it is for the Trial Bench to make that decision, and the Trial Bench -- that order composing the Trial Bench is Judge Parker presiding, Judge Van Den Wyngaert and myself; and in order for this to proceed in an orderly manner and also in the defence of Mr. Krstevski to make whatever submissions they want in response to the motion to withdraw, I suggest, Mr. Saxon, that you make this motion in writing and do it not later than Monday next week. And whatever response is needed from your side, Mr. Kemperdick, should be submitted not later than Thursday of next week. Do the parties have any questions regarding this? Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Kemperdick.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEMPERDICK
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What is then remaining here pending a decision on the now indicated motions or motion for withdrawal of the indictment is for me to make clear that until a decision on the question of detention or remand is made, Mr. Krstevski is to remain in custody. And also, before we adjourn, I would like to inquire, Mr. Krstevski, if there is any matter you would like to raise at this point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Kemperdick, do you want to add something to that "no"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEMPERDICK
utterances.text: It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may sit down, Mr. Krstevski. Mr. Kemperdick, stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kemperdick. I'm sure that all the questions surrounding the testimony, as such, will be addressed at the point when Mr. Krstevski is to appear before the Trial Bench who is to hear his testimony, but we have taken note of what you have now said. Mr. Saxon, before we adjourn, do you have anything to raise at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Well, with this, we now stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: at 2.24 p.m.
